text: Scope note: the original ask listed 7 tickets with "1 PR each". Your lane is IR-6586 only. Each of the other six has its own lane, so leaving them out is pre-approved and you don't need to ask.

Proceed with your plan. The ticket calls this mismatch the real problem and names a read-only check as a fast fix, so a warning fits. Constraints:
1) Make it best-effort. If the status-page lookup fails, the update still succeeds with its normal exit code. At most, print a debug note.
2) Print the warning to stderr only, so JSON/--output stays clean on stdout.
3) Fire it whenever the update leaves the incident resolved, and on any other command in the CLI that resolves an incident.
4) List each open event with its status page and the exact `rootly status-pages events resolve <id>` command to run.
5) Don't auto-resolve and don't rename anything.
6) Lane ir-6585-694b70 (IR-6585) is changing internal/cmd/incidents/update.go at the same time. Put the check in its own file or helper and add only a one-line call in update.go to keep merge conflicts small.
In the PR body, note that rootly-cli#57 already covered the requested commands under `status-pages events`.

Scope question on IR-6586: Should incident resolution ever resolve open status page entries automatically (or via an opt-in flag)? → go with: No: warn only, default behaviour unchanged. Resolving a public status page entry is a customer-visible write that can notify subscribers. The ticket asks for the mismatch to be visible, not for automatic resolves. Don't add an opt-in flag in this PR either. The warning already prints the exact `status-pages events resolve <id>` command to run. Mention an opt-in flag as a possible follow-up in the PR.

IR-6586: the lane proposes leaving 2 parts of the ask out of this run. Approve the cut? Approve with a reason ("approve: <why>"); the cut and the reason are printed on the PR. → approve: both cuts match what I already decided. (1) The requested write commands already shipped as `status-pages events create/update/resolve` in rootly-cli#57 (v0.6.1). Renaming them or adding an `incidents` alias would break released users, so no rename. (2) Resolving public status page entries automatically is a customer-visible product decision. This PR makes the mismatch visible with a warning to stderr that lists open events and the exact resolve command, and it does not resolve anything. Mention an opt-in flag as a possible follow-up.
